summary: Reviewed 5 modified files (config.ts, repositories.ts, index.ts, config.test.ts, repositories.test.ts). Full OWASP Top 10 scan performed. 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 2 Medium observations recorded (audit log information-disclosure boundary and Source namespace collision risk). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: OWASP A01 (Broken Access Control) — No issues. All credential mutation endpoints operate on server-local config with no multi-tenant isolation boundary. Access control is delegated to the OS-level binding (127.0.0.1 only, index.ts:180). This is consistent with the single-user local-tool architecture. No IDOR or path traversal vectors identified.

OWASP A02 (Cryptographic Failures) — Tokens stored in plaintext in config.json. The saveConfigField() function applies chmod 0o600 (config.ts:301) on POSIX to restrict file access to the owner, which is the appropriate mitigation for a local developer tool. On Windows, no file-permission tightening is applied (the platform check is explicit). This is a known, accepted architectural decision for this tool class. Recommend documenting the Windows gap in the security model and considering Credential Manager integration as a future improvement.

OWASP A02 (Token masking) — maskToken() (config.ts:29-31) exposes the last 4 characters of the token. For tokens shorter than 4 characters the full token is masked ('****'). For longer tokens, '****' + last-4 is returned. This leaks the tail of short tokens (e.g. 5-char token 'abcde' → '****e'). For PATs this is generally acceptable; however, if very short tokens are supported, even a single revealed character could aid brute-force. Low risk in practice but worth noting.

OWASP A03 (Injection) — No injection vectors found. All user-controlled strings (label, host, token, id, credentialId) are validated as non-empty strings and stored as-is in JSON (handled by JSON.stringify in writeJsonFile). Token injection into git URLs uses WHATWG URL property assignment (git-credentials.ts:79), which auto-encodes special characters — URL injection is not possible. Credential IDs go through toKebabCase() before auto-generation and are stored/compared by exact match.

OWASP A04 (Insecure Design) — No unsafe defaults. errorLogManager is optional (defensive optional chaining ?.append) to preserve backward compatibility. Audit log fires only after successful persistence — there is no TOCTOU window between the credential operation and the audit entry. The ordering (persist → audit) is correct: a failed write will throw before audit, preventing ghost audit entries for failed operations.

OWASP A05 (Security Misconfiguration) — Server binds to 127.0.0.1 only (index.ts:180), not 0.0.0.0. No CORS headers are emitted. Error responses return user-friendly messages without stack traces (sendError passes err.message for user-originated parse errors, but 500 paths return a generic 'Internal server error.' string). No verbose internals leak identified.

OWASP A06 (Vulnerable & Outdated Components) — No new third-party dependencies were introduced by this WP. All changes are internal route handler additions using existing in-tree modules (ErrorLogManager, saveConfigField, parseJsonBody, sendJson, sendError). No CVE surface added.

OWASP A07 (Identification & Authentication Failures) — This is a local single-user tool with no authentication layer; this is by design and within the tool's threat model. No session management, rate limiting, or credential storage vulnerabilities were introduced by this WP.

OWASP A08 (Software & Data Integrity) — No deserialization of untrusted data. JSON is parsed via parseJsonBody which enforces isPlainObject() before any field extraction. No prototype pollution vectors found (spread syntax used on validated plain objects only).

OWASP A09 (Security Logging & Monitoring Failures) — QA handoff raised three traceability questions; addressing each: (1) Source: 'credential-audit' is a custom string that does not collide with existing error-level Sources (e.g. 'GitManager', 'WorkspaceOrchestrator'). However, the Severity is set to 'warning' — if the ErrorLogManager GUI filters by Severity to separate operational errors from audit events, audit entries will appear in warning-level views alongside non-security warnings. No dedicated 'audit' Severity type exists in ErrorSeverity (error | warning). This is a medium traceability gap, not a blocking security issue. (2) errorLogManager absence in production: startServer() always instantiates ErrorLogManager (index.ts:96) and passes it to both route registrations. The optional parameter path is only reachable in test scenarios — the production code path always has the manager present. (3) Context field omission: create/update/delete entries use Context:{} while assign/clear entries use Context:{RepositoryId:id}. The ErrorLogContext interface has all fields optional, so empty Context is valid. Filtering by RepositoryId in the GUI will not surface config-level credential mutations; this is a monitoring completeness gap (not a security vulnerability). Recommend as a future improvement: add a dedicated 'audit' severity level or a flag to distinguish security audit events from operational warnings.

OWASP A10 (SSRF) — No server-side URL fetching is performed in the modified endpoints. The host field in credential entries is stored as a plain string and used only for host-matching at credential resolution time (git-credentials.ts:extractHost). The webserverUrl PUT endpoint (config.ts:460-464) blocks javascript:, data:, and vbscript: schemes. No SSRF vector introduced by this WP.

Token absence verification — Confirmed by code inspection and test coverage. The audit log append() calls in config.ts:287-293 and config.ts:332-338 reference savedEntry.id, savedEntry.label, savedEntry.host and deletedEntry.id, deletedEntry.label, deletedEntry.host — never .token. The repositories.ts:291-300 audit entries reference only the credentialId (the ID string, not the token value). The dedicated test at config.test.ts:1473-1495 confirms no token leakage via JSON serialization of the audit entry.

summary: Reviewed all 5 modified files: config.ts, repositories.ts, index.ts, config.test.ts, repositories.test.ts.

Architecture: errorLogManager is cleanly threaded as an optional parameter at every call site. Optional chaining (?.append) is consistently applied — no crash risk when the manager is absent. Backward compatibility is fully preserved.

Audit log placement (persist → audit ordering) is correct: early-return guards precede all append() calls, and persistence is always attempted before auditing. No ghost audit entries for failed writes.

Token safety: exhaustive code inspection confirms no credential token value is referenced in any append() call across config.ts and repositories.ts. The dedicated token-absence test (config.test.ts:1473–1495) serializes the entire entry to JSON and asserts the raw token string is absent.

Test quality: MockErrorLogManager in both test files is structurally identical — a clean, minimal stub pattern. Tests cover all 5 mutation paths with Source and Operation assertions. The flushAsync() helper usage in repositories.test.ts improves tick-flushing readability over the double-nextTick pattern in config.test.ts.

One documentation-forward item recorded: the inline ternary in config.ts:292 Message construction and the pre-existing token-mask inconsistency between credential-options ('***' hardcoded) and the maskToken() helper ('****' + last-4). Neither was introduced by this WP.
No blocking issues found. No behavioral changes applied. PASS verdict.

comments.note: config.ts:292 — The audit Message uses an inline ternary (auditOperation === 'create-credential' ? 'created' : 'updated') to derive the past-tense verb. This duplicates logic already captured in auditOperation. A future refactor could derive the verb from a small lookup map (e.g. const verb = { 'create-credential': 'created', 'update-credential': 'updated' }[auditOperation]) to make the message template uniform. Not applied as Fix-Forward because even a cosmetic message change would alter persisted audit log content.

[documentation-forward] The GET /api/repositories/:id/credential-options endpoint in repositories.ts:350 masks tokens with the hardcoded string '***' (3 asterisks), while the config.ts maskToken() helper produces '****' + last-4 chars (4 asterisks prefix). This inconsistency is pre-existing and was not introduced by this WP, but it means the two credential-listing surfaces return tokens in different masked formats. The Documentation agent should note this discrepancy in the API surface documentation and flag it as a known inconsistency pending a future cleanup pass.

config.test.ts:1420–1421 uses two sequential 'await new Promise(resolve => process.nextTick(resolve))' calls for async tick-flushing, while repositories.test.ts uses the cleaner 'await flushAsync()' helper (which appears to be a shared utility). Consider migrating config.test.ts to use flushAsync() for consistency and readability. This is a test-quality observation, not a production code concern.

The MockErrorLogManager stub is duplicated verbatim between config.test.ts:80–89 and repositories.test.ts:112–121. Both implement the same appendedEntries array and append() stub. A shared test helper module (e.g. src/server/__tests__/helpers/mock-error-log-manager.ts) would eliminate duplication and keep the stub interface in sync when ErrorLogManager evolves.

Security Auditor noted (OWASP A09) that audit entries use Severity: 'warning' because the ErrorSeverity type only supports 'error' | 'warning'. This is architecturally sound given current type constraints. The Principal Systems Architect endorses the Security Auditor's recommendation: if a dedicated 'audit' severity is added to ErrorSeverity in a future iteration, all credential-audit append() calls in config.ts and repositories.ts should be updated to use it. This would allow GUI-level filtering to cleanly separate security audit events from operational warnings without relying on Source-string filtering.
